source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 11 (PDF 234-257, printed 231-254); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 11 (Human Circulatory System), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.
11.1 Structure and functioning of the heart

blocks.prompt: 1 The closed blood circulatory system of humans consists of:

options.text: lymph, lymph nodes and lymph vessels

blocks.explanation: The closed blood circulatory system consists of blood, heart and blood vessels (arteries, capillaries and veins) (11.1).

book_ref.quote: The closed blood circulatory system of humans consists of blood, heart

blocks.prompt: 2 In a healthy person, plasma makes up about what share of blood by volume?
blocks.explanation: Plasma is about 55% and cells or cell-like bodies about 45% of blood by volume (11.1).

book_ref.quote: plasma constitutes about 55% by volume of the blood

blocks.prompt: 3 The human heart is situated:

options.text: in the middle of the chest cavity, between the lungs
in the left side of the abdominal cavity

blocks.explanation: The heart lies in the middle of the chest cavity between the lungs; its back is near the vertebral column and its front behind the sternum (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It is situated in the middle of chest cavity (between the lungs).

blocks.prompt: 4 Because the heart lies between the lungs:

options.text: the right lung is smaller and has a cardiac notch
the left lung is smaller and has a cardiac notch
both lungs are equal in size
the left lung has no lobes

blocks.explanation: The left lung is smaller than the right and has a cardiac notch in its border to accommodate the heart (11.1).

book_ref.quote: has a cardiac notch in its border to accommodate the heart

blocks.prompt: 5 The sac that encloses the heart and separates it from surrounding organs is the:
blocks.explanation: The heart is enclosed in the pericardium, which separates it from surrounding organs (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Heart is enclosed in a sac called pericardium

blocks.prompt: 6 The fibrous pericardium protects the heart against external pressure and shocks and also:

options.text: prevents excessive dilation of the heart

blocks.explanation: The outer fibrous pericardium, of strong connective tissue, protects the heart and prevents excessive dilation (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It also prevents excessive dilation of heart.

blocks.prompt: 7 The visceral pericardium, closely attached to the heart, is also called:
blocks.explanation: The serous pericardium has an outer parietal layer and an inner visceral layer, also called epicardium (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Inner visceral pericardium (also called epicardium)

blocks.prompt: 8 The pericardial cavity between parietal and visceral pericardium contains:
blocks.explanation: The pericardial cavity contains up to 50 mL pericardial fluid, which lubricates the heart and protects it from infections (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It contains up to 50 mL pericardial fluid.

blocks.prompt: 9 The thickest layer of the heart wall, made of cardiac muscles, is the:
blocks.explanation: Beneath the epicardium lies the myocardium, the thickest layer, made of cardiac muscles (11.1).

book_ref.quote: the thickest layer of heart wall i.e., myocardium

blocks.prompt: 10 The endocardium is:

options.text: the outer lining of the heart wall
a thick layer of cardiac muscles
a fibrous sac around the heart
a single layer of epithelial cells lining the heart chambers

blocks.explanation: The endocardium lies beneath the myocardium; it is a single layer of epithelial cells lining the heart chambers (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It is a single layer of epithelial cells and make the inner linings

blocks.prompt: 11 The two upper, thin-walled chambers of the heart are the:
blocks.explanation: The heart has two upper thin-walled atria that receive blood and two lower thick-walled ventricles that distribute it (11.1).

book_ref.quote: two upper thin-walled atria and two lower thick-walled ventricles

blocks.prompt: 12 The septum that separates the left and right ventricles and is much thicker than the interatrial septum is the:
blocks.explanation: The interventricular septum separates the ventricles and is much thicker than the interatrial septum (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It is much thicker than the interatrial septum.

blocks.prompt: 13 The mitral valve is another name for the:
blocks.explanation: The bicuspid (mitral) valve, made of two cusps, lies between the left atrium and left ventricle (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Bicuspid (mitral) valve (made of two cusps)

blocks.prompt: 14 The valves at the exit points of the ventricles, shaped like a half-moon, are the:
blocks.explanation: Two semilunar valves (pulmonary and aortic) lie at the exits of the ventricles (11.1).

book_ref.quote: At the exit points of ventricles, there are two semilunar valves

blocks.prompt: 15 The pulmonary and aortic valves close when:
blocks.explanation: When the ventricles relax, the pulmonary and aortic valves close and stop backflow from the pulmonary artery and aorta into the ventricles (11.1).

book_ref.quote: When ventricles relax, pulmonary and aortic valves close.

blocks.prompt: 16 The tricuspid and bicuspid valves are located in the:

options.text: atrioventricular septum, at the entrance points of the ventricles

blocks.explanation: The two atrioventricular valves lie at the entrance points of the ventricles, in the atrioventricular septum (11.1).

book_ref.quote: At the entrance points of ventricles (in atrioventricular septum)

blocks.prompt: 17 The human heart is called a double pump because it:

options.text: beats twice in each cardiac cycle
carries out both pulmonary and systemic circulation

blocks.explanation: The heart carries out pulmonary circulation (to lungs) and systemic circulation (to all organs except lungs) (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Human heart functions as a double pump.

blocks.prompt: 18 The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body through the:
blocks.explanation: Deoxygenated blood reaches the right atrium through the superior and inferior vena cava (11.1).

book_ref.quote: via two veins i.e., superior vena cava and inferior vena cava

blocks.prompt: 19 The pulmonary trunk divides into:
blocks.explanation: The pulmonary trunk divides into left and right pulmonary arteries carrying deoxygenated blood to the lungs (11.1).

book_ref.quote: The pulmonary trunk divides into left and right pulmonary arteries

blocks.prompt: 20 Oxygenated blood from the lungs is brought to the left atrium by the:
blocks.explanation: Pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium (11.1).

book_ref.quote: The oxygenated blood from lungs is brought to left atrium by pulmonary veins.

blocks.prompt: 21 The wall of the left ventricle is about how many times thicker than that of the right ventricle?
blocks.explanation: The left ventricle wall is about 3 times thicker because it pushes blood all over the body (11.1).

book_ref.quote: thicker (about 3 times) than that of the right ventricle

blocks.prompt: 22 The relaxed period of the heart chambers, when the atria fill with blood, is called:
blocks.explanation: When atria and ventricles are both relaxed and the atria fill with blood, the period is diastole (11.1).

book_ref.quote: This relaxed period of heart chambers is called diastole.

blocks.prompt: 23 Ventricular systole pumps blood into the:
blocks.explanation: When the filled ventricles contract (ventricular systole), blood is pumped to the pulmonary arteries and aorta (11.1).

book_ref.quote: This is called ventricular systole and it pumps the blood

blocks.prompt: 24 In one complete heartbeat, diastole lasts about:
blocks.explanation: Diastole lasts about 0.4 s, atrial systole about 0.1 s and ventricular systole about 0.3 s (11.1).

book_ref.quote: diastole lasts about 0.4 sec

blocks.prompt: 25 In one complete heartbeat, ventricular systole lasts about:
blocks.explanation: Ventricular systole lasts about 0.3 s; atrial systole about 0.1 s; diastole about 0.4 s (11.1).

book_ref.quote: the ventricular systole lasts about 0.3 sec

blocks.prompt: 26 In one's life, the heart beats about:
blocks.explanation: In one's life the heart beats about 2.5 billion times without stopping (11.1).

book_ref.quote: heart beats about 2.5 billion times

blocks.prompt: 27 The 'dubb' sound of the heartbeat is produced when:

options.text: the tricuspid and bicuspid valves close
the pulmonary and aortic semilunar valves close as the ventricles relax

blocks.explanation: When ventricular systole ends and the ventricles relax, the semilunar valves close and make the 'dubb' sound (11.1).

book_ref.quote: the pulmonary and aortic semilunar valves close and

blocks.prompt: 28 The 'lubb-dubb' sounds of the heart can be heard with a:
blocks.explanation: Lubb-dubb can be heard with the help of a stethoscope (11.1).

book_ref.quote: can be heard with the help of a stethoscope

blocks.prompt: 29 A heart murmur is heard when:

options.text: the heart rate falls during sleep
the valves do not close fully or open narrowly, creating turbulence

blocks.explanation: If valves do not close fully or open narrowly, turbulence is created; it is heard as a murmur, which sounds like a hiss (11.1).

book_ref.quote: turbulence is created within the heart

blocks.prompt: 30 Serious heart murmurs can be corrected by:

options.text: replacing the damaged valves with artificial or donor valves

blocks.explanation: Most murmurs are not serious; serious ones can be corrected by replacing damaged valves with artificial ones or valves from an organ donor (11.1).

book_ref.quote: replacing the damaged valves with artificial ones

blocks.prompt: 31 The sinoatrial (SA) node consists of:

options.text: a bundle of nerve fibres from the brain
a small cluster of cardiac muscle cells

blocks.explanation: The SA node (pacemaker) is a small cluster of cardiac muscle cells in the upper wall of the right atrium (11.1).

book_ref.quote: The sinoatrial node consists of a small cluster of cardiac muscle cells.

blocks.prompt: 32 The atrioventricular (AV) node lies at the:

options.text: upper wall of the right atrium
lower portion of the interatrial septum

blocks.explanation: The AV node, also a small cluster of cardiac muscle cells, lies at the lower portion of the interatrial septum (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It lies at the lower portion of interatrial septum.

blocks.prompt: 33 The atrioventricular bundle (bundle of His) is a network of fibres present in the:
blocks.explanation: From the AV node impulses reach the bundle of His, a network of fibres in the interventricular septum (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It is a network of fibres present in interventricular septum.

blocks.prompt: 34 The left and right branches of the AV bundle end at the:

options.text: Purkinje fibres in the ventricle walls

blocks.explanation: The AV bundle branches end at the Purkinje fibres; their stimulation makes the ventricles contract almost simultaneously (11.1).

book_ref.quote: which end at the Purkinje fibres in the walls of the ventricles

blocks.prompt: 35 The delay of about 0.15 second in conduction of impulses from the SA node to the AV node:

options.text: makes the atria and ventricles contract together
lets atrial systole finish before ventricular systole begins

blocks.explanation: The 0.15 s delay permits atrial systole to be completed before ventricular systole begins (11.1).

book_ref.quote: There is a delay of about 0.15 second

blocks.prompt: 36 An artificial pacemaker is used in patients whose:
blocks.explanation: In patients with a weak SA node, a battery-operated artificial pacemaker emits electrical signals that trigger normal heartbeats (11.1).

book_ref.quote: In such patients of weak SA node, artificial pacemaker is used.

blocks.prompt: 37 The heart of an average adult beats about:
blocks.explanation: The average adult heart beats about 70 times per minute (11.1).

book_ref.quote: The heart of an average adult beats about 70 times per minute.

blocks.prompt: 38 During fever and exercise, the heart rate increases because:

options.text: the brain's control centre sends nerve signals to the pacemaker and AV node
ANH is secreted by the right atrium

blocks.explanation: In fever and exercise the brain's control centre signals the pacemaker and AV node to increase the rate; at rest it slows them (11.1).

book_ref.quote: during fever and exercise, the control centre in brain sends nerve signals

blocks.prompt: 39 In an adult, every day about 8,000 litres of blood move through:
blocks.explanation: About 8,000 litres of blood move through 96,000 km of blood vessels every day (11.1).

book_ref.quote: about 8,000 litres of blood move through 96,000 km

blocks.prompt: 40 An electrocardiogram (ECG) is a recording of:

options.text: electrical potentials generated by the currents of cardiac impulses

blocks.explanation: ECG records the electrical potentials generated by the currents of cardiac impulses, using electrodes on the skin (11.1).

book_ref.quote: is known as electrocardiogram (ECG)

blocks.prompt: 41 The machine that records the electrical potentials of the heart is the:
blocks.explanation: Electrodes on the skin are attached to an electrocardiograph, which records the potentials (11.1).

book_ref.quote: The electrodes are attached to a machine called electrocardiograph

blocks.prompt: 42 In an ECG, the P wave shows:
blocks.explanation: The P wave shows the beginning of atrial depolarization, initiated by the SA node; it causes atrial contraction (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It shows beginning of atrial depolarization, initiated by SA node.

blocks.prompt: 43 Irregular or absent P waves may indicate:
blocks.explanation: Irregular or absent P waves may indicate arrhythmia, a lack of rhythmicity (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Irregular or absent P waves may indicate arrhythmia

blocks.prompt: 44 A first-degree heart block is shown in the ECG by:

options.text: a PR interval longer than 0.20 seconds

blocks.explanation: Book correction: the normal PR interval is 0.12-0.20 s; first-degree heart block is a prolonged PR interval of more than 0.20 s (11.1).

book_ref.quote: A first-degree heart block is a prolonged PR interval (more than 0.20 seconds).

blocks.prompt: 45 Atrial repolarization occurs during the ECG phase called:
blocks.explanation: QRS shows the beginning of ventricular depolarization; atrial repolarization also occurs during this phase (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Atrial re-polarization also occurs during this phase.

blocks.prompt: 46 The ST segment is elevated in:
blocks.explanation: The ST segment can be depressed in ischemia and elevated in myocardial infarction (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It can be depressed in ischemia

blocks.prompt: 47 The ST segment of an ECG ordinarily lasts about:
blocks.explanation: The ST segment shows completion of ventricular depolarization and lasts about 0.08 s (11.1).

book_ref.quote: This segment ordinarily lasts about 0.08 second.

blocks.prompt: 48 The T wave of an ECG represents:

options.text: the beginning of repolarization of ventricles

blocks.explanation: The T wave represents the beginning of ventricular repolarization; T wave abnormalities may show electrolyte disturbance (11.1).

book_ref.quote: It represents the beginning of repolarization of ventricles.

blocks.prompt: 49 A normal QT interval, from the beginning of QRS to the end of the T wave, is usually about:
blocks.explanation: A normal QT interval is usually about 0.40 s (11.1).

book_ref.quote: A normal QT interval is usually about 0.40 seconds.

blocks.prompt: 50 Blue babies (cyanosis) can result from failure of the:

options.text: interatrial foramen to close during development

blocks.explanation: Cyanosis results when the interatrial foramen fails to close, mixing oxygenated and deoxygenated blood between the atria (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Cyanosis results due to the failure of interatrial foramen to close

blocks.prompt: 51 The ductus arteriosus is a temporary channel in the embryo between the:
blocks.explanation: The ductus arteriosus joins the embryonic pulmonary artery and aorta; normally it constricts during development (11.1).

book_ref.quote: Ductus arteriosus is a temporary channel between the embryonic pulmonary artery and aorta.

blocks.prompt: 52 Which arteries carry deoxygenated blood?
blocks.explanation: All arteries carry oxygenated blood except the pulmonary arteries (11.2).

book_ref.quote: All arteries carry oxygenated blood, except pulmonary arteries.

blocks.prompt: 53 The outer layer of an artery wall is called:
blocks.explanation: Artery wall: outer tunica externa (adventitia) of connective and elastic tissue, middle tunica media, inner tunica intima (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Outer layer i.e., tunica externa or adventitia

blocks.prompt: 54 The tunica media of an artery, made of thick muscular tissue and elastic fibres, helps the artery to:

options.text: withstand higher blood pressure during ventricular systole

blocks.explanation: The middle layer can withstand the higher blood pressure during ventricular systole (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Middle layer is important and it can withstand higher blood pressure

blocks.prompt: 55 The tunica intima of an artery is made of:

options.text: a thin layer of endothelial cells

blocks.explanation: The inner tunica intima is a thin layer of endothelial cells (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Inner layer i.e., tunica intima is made of thin layer of endothelial cells.

blocks.prompt: 56 The walls of capillaries are made of:

options.text: a single layer of endothelial cells

blocks.explanation: Capillary walls are a single layer of endothelial cells, so materials are exchanged between blood and tissues (11.2).

book_ref.quote: The walls of capillaries are made of a single layer of endothelial cells.

blocks.prompt: 57 The internal diameter of a capillary is about:
blocks.explanation: A capillary is about 8 micrometres across, so narrow that RBCs pass in single line (11.2).

book_ref.quote: The internal diameter of a capillary is about 8 micrometres.

blocks.prompt: 58 No cell of the body is more than how far away from a capillary?
blocks.explanation: No body cell is more than 100 micrometres away from a capillary (11.2).

book_ref.quote: No cell of the body is more than 100 micrometres away from a capillary.

blocks.prompt: 59 Capillaries are so narrow that:

options.text: no WBC can ever leave them
RBCs must pass through them in single line

blocks.explanation: Capillaries are so narrow that RBCs pass through in single line (11.2).

book_ref.quote: RBCs must pass through them in single line

blocks.prompt: 60 The total length of capillaries in an adult human is estimated to be over:
blocks.explanation: The total length of capillaries in an adult is over 80,600 km, enough to encircle the globe twice (11.2).

book_ref.quote: total length of capillaries in an adult human is over 80,600 kilometres

blocks.prompt: 61 When interstitial fluid leaks out of capillaries, which remain inside the capillaries?
blocks.explanation: Interstitial fluid has water, nutrients, hormones, gases, wastes and small proteins; large proteins, RBCs and platelets stay in capillaries (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Large proteins, RBCs and platelets remain within capillaries.

blocks.prompt: 62 Some materials are taken up by capillary wall cells and passed to the other side by:
blocks.explanation: Some materials enter capillary wall cells by endocytosis and are passed to the other side by exocytosis (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Some materials are also taken up by capillary wall cells by endocytosis.

blocks.prompt: 63 Which veins carry oxygenated blood?
blocks.explanation: All veins carry deoxygenated blood except the pulmonary veins (11.2).

book_ref.quote: All veins carry deoxygenated blood, except pulmonary veins.

blocks.prompt: 64 An empty vein collapses like an empty balloon because:

options.text: it has a thick tunica media
it is made of a single layer of cells
its tunica media is relatively thin and only slightly muscular

blocks.explanation: The vein's middle layer is thin with few elastic fibres, since veins do not withstand high pressure; an empty artery stays hollow (11.2).

book_ref.quote: an empty vein collapses like an empty balloon

blocks.prompt: 65 Semilunar valves in veins:

options.text: prevent the back flow of blood moving towards the heart

blocks.explanation: Semilunar valves in veins prevent backflow of blood as it moves towards the heart (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Semilunar valves are present in veins to prevent the back flow of blood

blocks.prompt: 66 The return of blood in veins towards the heart is assisted by:

options.text: pressure from contraction of surrounding muscles
high pressure from the left ventricle
the elastic tunica media of veins

blocks.explanation: Contraction of surrounding muscles presses veins and assists the return of blood towards the heart (11.2).

book_ref.quote: The pressure generated by the contraction of surrounding muscles presses veins

blocks.prompt: 67 Which chemical can dilate capillaries?
blocks.explanation: Nervous stimulation can constrict capillaries and chemicals such as histamine can dilate them (11.2).

book_ref.quote: certain chemicals such as histamine can dilate them

blocks.prompt: 68 A pre-capillary sphincter is:

options.text: a node in the heart wall
a ring of muscles guarding the entry of a capillary loop
a layer of the artery wall

blocks.explanation: The entry of each capillary loop is guarded by a ring of muscles, the pre-capillary sphincter, which regulates blood flow through capillaries (11.2).

book_ref.quote: The entry of each loop is guarded by a ring of muscles called a pre-capillary sphincter.

blocks.prompt: 69 The walls of arterioles contain:

options.text: more circular muscles than elastic tissue
more elastic tissue than circular muscles

blocks.explanation: Arteriole walls have more circular muscles than elastic tissue; their contraction narrows the arterioles (11.2).

book_ref.quote: In the walls of arterioles, there are more circular muscles than elastic tissue.

blocks.prompt: 70 The contraction of the circular muscles of arterioles is controlled by the:
blocks.explanation: Arteriole muscles are under nervous and endocrine control; contraction is vasoconstriction, relaxation is vasodilation (11.2).

book_ref.quote: under the control of nervous and endocrine systems

blocks.prompt: 71 When metabolic activity in a tissue rises, its arterioles:

options.text: dilate, because oxygen falls and carbon dioxide rises in its interstitial fluid

blocks.explanation: Rising activity lowers O₂ and raises CO₂ in interstitial fluid; arteriole muscles relax (vasodilation), bringing more O₂ and removing more CO₂ (11.2).

book_ref.quote: when metabolic activity in a tissue rises, oxygen decreases

blocks.prompt: 72 The velocity of blood flow in the aorta is about:
blocks.explanation: Velocity is highest in the aorta (450-500 mm/s), lowest in capillaries (1 mm/s) and rises again in veins and vena cavae (250-300 mm/s) (11.2).

book_ref.quote: It is highest in aorta (450-500 mm/sec)

blocks.prompt: 73 The velocity of blood in the vena cavae is about:
blocks.explanation: Blood velocity rises again in venules, veins and vena cavae to about 250-300 mm/s (11.2).

book_ref.quote: veins and vena cavae (250-300 mm/sec)

blocks.prompt: 74 The changes in velocity of blood in different vessels result from changes in:

options.text: the total cross section of the vessel system

blocks.explanation: Velocity changes result from changes in the total cross section of the vessel system (11.2).

book_ref.quote: These changes in the velocity of blood result from changes in the total cross section

blocks.prompt: 75 Blood circulating in two main pathways, pulmonary and systemic, is found in humans and in all:
blocks.explanation: In humans and in all mammals and birds blood circulates in two main pathways: pulmonary and systemic (11.2).

book_ref.quote: In humans (and in all mammals and birds), blood circulates throughout body in two main pathways.

blocks.prompt: 76 In pulmonary circulation, blood is oxygenated in the:
blocks.explanation: The pulmonary arteries branch into arterioles and lung capillaries, where blood is oxygenated (11.2).

book_ref.quote: In lung capillaries, blood is oxygenated.

blocks.prompt: 77 In pulmonary circulation, the left and right pulmonary veins open into the:
blocks.explanation: Lung capillaries join into pulmonary venules and veins, which open into the left atrium (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Left and right pulmonary veins from lungs open in left atrium.

blocks.prompt: 78 The right and left coronary arteries arise from the:
blocks.explanation: Two coronary arteries arise from the aorta near its origin and supply the heart walls (11.2).

book_ref.quote: arise from aorta, near its origin

blocks.prompt: 79 The coronary veins join to form the coronary sinus, which opens into the:
blocks.explanation: Coronary veins join to form the coronary sinus, which opens into the right atrium; small coronary veins drain directly there (11.2).

book_ref.quote: The coronary veins join to form a coronary sinus

blocks.prompt: 80 A portal system is a circulation in which:
blocks.explanation: In a portal system veins end in capillaries, e.g. the hepatic portal vein ending in the liver (11.2).

book_ref.quote: A portal system is a circulation in which veins end in capillaries.

blocks.prompt: 81 The hepatic portal vein collects blood from the:
blocks.explanation: The hepatic portal vein collects blood from the spleen and alimentary canal and takes it to the liver (11.2).

book_ref.quote: a large hepatic portal vein collects blood from spleen and alimentary canal

blocks.prompt: 82 The hepatic portal system extends from the:

options.text: lower portion of the oesophagus to the upper part of the anal canal

blocks.explanation: The hepatic portal system extends from the lower oesophagus to the upper anal canal (11.2).

book_ref.quote: extends from the lower portion of oesophagus to the upper part of anal canal

blocks.prompt: 83 In renal circulation, each afferent arteriole divides to make the:
blocks.explanation: Afferent arterioles supply nephrons; each forms glomerular capillaries, which unite into the efferent arteriole (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Each afferent arteriole divides to make the capillaries of glomeruli.

blocks.prompt: 84 The vasa recta are capillaries around the nephron tubule in the:
blocks.explanation: The efferent arteriole forms peri-tubular capillaries (cortex) and vasa recta (medulla) (11.2).

book_ref.quote: vasa recta (around nephron tubule in the medulla of kidney)

blocks.prompt: 85 Which of these is NOT present in humans?
blocks.explanation: Book correction: the printed figure is captioned 'Renal portal system', but humans have no renal portal system; it shows the renal circulation (11.2).

book_ref.quote: Humans have no renal portal system

blocks.prompt: 86 Blood pressure is the measure of:

options.text: the force exerted by blood against the inner walls of blood vessels
the volume of blood pumped per minute
the speed of blood in capillaries
the number of heartbeats per minute

blocks.explanation: Blood pressure is the force of blood against the inner walls of vessels; it keeps blood flowing to the capillary network (11.3).

book_ref.quote: Blood pressure is the measure of force exerted by blood against the inner walls

blocks.prompt: 87 The term blood pressure most commonly refers to:
blocks.explanation: Pressure occurs throughout the vascular system, but blood pressure usually means systemic arterial blood pressure (11.3).

book_ref.quote: most commonly refers to systemic arterial blood pressure

blocks.prompt: 88 The rhythmical throbbing of arteries created by the flow of blood is called:
blocks.explanation: Because artery walls are elastic, the flow of blood creates rhythmical throbbing called the pulse (11.3).

book_ref.quote: The flow of blood creates rhythmical throbbing of arteries

blocks.prompt: 89 Diastolic pressure in a normal young adult is:
blocks.explanation: Diastolic pressure, the lowest arterial pressure before the next ventricular contraction, is 75-85 mm Hg in a normal young adult (11.3).

book_ref.quote: Diastolic pressure in a normal young adult is 75-85 mm Hg.

blocks.prompt: 90 The instrument used for manual measurement of systolic and diastolic pressures is the:
blocks.explanation: A sphygmomanometer measures blood pressure; the rise and fall of its mercury column shows the readings (11.3).

book_ref.quote: The instrument sphygmomanometer is used for the manual measurement

blocks.prompt: 91 Baroreceptors (pressure receptors) are present in the:
blocks.explanation: Baroreceptors are in the carotid arteries (supplying head and brain) and the aortic arch (11.3).

book_ref.quote: are present in carotid arteries

blocks.prompt: 92 When blood volume and pressure decrease, receptors in the brain stimulate the posterior pituitary to secrete:
blocks.explanation: Low blood volume and pressure make brain receptors create thirst and stimulate the posterior pituitary to secrete ADH (11.3).

book_ref.quote: stimulate posterior pituitary gland to secrete antidiuretic hormone (ADH)

blocks.prompt: 93 ADH raises blood volume and pressure by:

options.text: speeding up excretion of salts and water
making the kidneys retain more water and constricting arterioles

blocks.explanation: ADH makes kidneys retain more water, excreting less in urine; it also constricts arterioles, raising arterial pressure (11.3).

book_ref.quote: ADH stimulates kidneys to retain more water in blood

blocks.prompt: 94 Atrial natriuretic hormone (ANH) is secreted by endocrine cells in the walls of the:
blocks.explanation: Endocrine cells in the right atrium wall secrete ANH when the atrium is stretched by increased blood volume (11.3).

book_ref.quote: The walls of right atrium contain endocrine cells

blocks.prompt: 95 ANH lowers blood volume and pressure by:

options.text: speeding up excretion of salts and water through urine

blocks.explanation: ANH speeds up excretion of salts and water in urine, lowering blood volume and pressure (11.3).

book_ref.quote: It speeds up the excretion of salts and water through urine

blocks.prompt: 96 The prime contributor to atherosclerosis is thought to be the accumulation of:
blocks.explanation: Fatty materials, smooth muscle cells, cholesterol, fibrin and debris may accumulate in arteries; cholesterol is thought to be the prime contributor (11.4).

book_ref.quote: The accumulation of cholesterol is thought to be the prime contributor to atherosclerosis.

blocks.prompt: 97 Arteriosclerosis (hardening of arterial walls) occurs when:

options.text: a thrombus forms in the brain
calcium is deposited in arterial walls

blocks.explanation: Arteriosclerosis is hardening of arterial walls due to calcium deposits; arteries cannot expand and the heart works harder (11.4).

book_ref.quote: It occurs when calcium is deposited in arterial walls.

blocks.prompt: 98 Severe atherosclerosis usually leads to:
blocks.explanation: Severe atherosclerosis usually leads to arteriosclerosis (11.4).

book_ref.quote: Severe atherosclerosis usually leads to arteriosclerosis.

blocks.prompt: 99 In coronary angiography, the special fluid injected through the catheter so it shows on X-ray is called:
blocks.explanation: When the catheter tip reaches the coronary openings, a contrast medium (dye) is injected; it is visible on X-ray and gives angiograms (11.4).

book_ref.quote: a special fluid (called a contrast medium or dye) is injected in catheter

blocks.prompt: 100 In an angiogram, a coronary artery with clots in its lumen appears:
blocks.explanation: If clots are present in the lumen of a coronary artery, it appears narrow in the angiogram (11.4).

book_ref.quote: If clots are present in the lumen of a coronary artery, the artery appears narrow.

blocks.prompt: 101 Myocardial infarction (heart attack) is the condition in which:

options.text: blood is retained in heart and lungs
heart muscles die due to no supply of oxygen and nutrients

blocks.explanation: If blocked coronary arteries leave heart muscle with no oxygen and nutrients and it dies, it is myocardial infarction (11.4).

book_ref.quote: the condition is known as myocardial infarction (heart attack)

blocks.prompt: 102 Blockage of coronary arteries is usually due to gradual build-up of:

options.text: lipids, especially cholesterol, in the inner wall

blocks.explanation: Coronary blockage is usually due to gradual build-up of lipids, especially cholesterol, in the inner wall of the artery (11.4).

book_ref.quote: gradual build-up of lipids (especially cholesterol)

blocks.prompt: 103 Angina pectoris indicates that:

options.text: the blood pressure is very low
the heart's oxygen demand is greater than its delivery

blocks.explanation: Angina is chest pain during stress or exertion; it shows oxygen demand exceeds delivery and a heart attack may follow (11.4).

book_ref.quote: Angina indicates that oxygen demands are greater than its delivery

blocks.prompt: 104 In coronary bypass surgery, the surgeon attaches a healthy blood vessel taken from the patient's:
blocks.explanation: A healthy vessel from leg, arm, chest or abdomen is attached above and below the blocked artery so blood bypasses the blockage (11.4).

book_ref.quote: takes a healthy blood vessel from leg, arm, chest or abdomen

blocks.prompt: 105 Even after a successful bypass surgery, the most crucial lifestyle change to reduce future blockages is:
blocks.explanation: Bypass does not cure atherosclerosis; lifestyle changes, especially smoking cessation, are crucial (11.4).

book_ref.quote: especially smoking cessation

blocks.prompt: 106 A stent used during angioplasty is:

options.text: an expandable stainless steel mesh tube
a healthy vein from the leg

blocks.explanation: A stent is an expandable stainless steel mesh tube on a balloon catheter; it stays in place and keeps the artery open (11.4).

book_ref.quote: A stent is an expandable stainless steel mesh tube

blocks.prompt: 107 In angioplasty, the small sausage-shaped balloon is inflated to:

options.text: dilate the narrowed section of the artery

blocks.explanation: The balloon is inflated to dilate the narrowed section; dye is then injected to confirm the dilatation (11.4).

book_ref.quote: The balloon is then inflated to dilate the narrowed section of the artery.

blocks.prompt: 108 After the artery is dilated in angioplasty, a small amount of dye is injected to:
blocks.explanation: Once the artery is dilated, dye is injected to confirm the successful dilatation (11.4).

book_ref.quote: a small amount of dye is injected to confirm the successful dilatation

blocks.prompt: 109 Hypertension occurs when blood pressure consistently remains above:
blocks.explanation: Hypertension is a chronic elevation of blood pressure, consistently above 140/90 (11.4).

book_ref.quote: It occurs when blood pressure consistently remains above 140/90.

blocks.prompt: 110 Rupture of blood vessels in the brain due to chronic high blood pressure is called:
blocks.explanation: Chronic high pressure raises the chance of vessel rupture; in the brain it is a brain haemorrhage (11.4).

book_ref.quote: When this occurs in brain, it is called brain haemorrhage.

blocks.prompt: 111 When prolonged hypertension makes the heart unable to pump effectively and blood is retained in the heart and lungs, the condition is:
blocks.explanation: Prolonged hypertension weakens the heart; blood is retained in heart and lungs: congestive heart failure (11.4).

book_ref.quote: It is called congestive heart failure.

blocks.prompt: 112 When hypertension damages the nephrons of the kidneys, it leads to:

options.text: loss of salts and lower pressure
formation of a renal portal system
more ANH secretion and low pressure
more retention of salts and water and further hypertension

blocks.explanation: Damaged nephrons retain more salts and water in blood, causing further hypertension (11.4).

book_ref.quote: Hypertension can also damage the nephrons of kidneys.

blocks.prompt: 113 A thrombus is:

options.text: a solid mass or plug of blood constituents (clot) in a blood vessel
a swelling of a lymph node
a deposit of calcium in an artery wall
a weak area in the heart valve

blocks.explanation: Thrombosis is formation of a thrombus, a solid clot of blood constituents in a vessel that may block it wholly or partly (11.4).

book_ref.quote: Thrombus is a solid mass or plug of blood constituents

blocks.prompt: 114 A thrombus in the blood vessels of the brain causes:
blocks.explanation: A thrombus in coronary arteries causes a heart attack; in brain vessels it causes a stroke (11.4).

book_ref.quote: a thrombus in the vessels of brain causes stroke

blocks.prompt: 115 Formation of a thrombus in a vessel and then its carriage to another location is called:
blocks.explanation: Formation of a thrombus and its carriage elsewhere is thromboembolism; the dislodged thrombus is an embolus (11.4).

book_ref.quote: Formation of thrombus in a blood vessel and then its carriage to any other location is called thromboembolism.

blocks.prompt: 116 Which of these can cause thrombus formation?

options.text: reduced blood flow due to long periods of inactivity

blocks.explanation: Thrombus may form due to irritation or infection of the vessel lining, reduced blood flow from long inactivity, or pneumonia, tuberculosis, emphysema (11.4).

book_ref.quote: reduced rate of blood flow, due to long periods of inactivity

blocks.prompt: 117 The lymphatic system consists of:

options.text: lymph vessels, lymphoid masses, lymph nodes and lymph

blocks.explanation: The lymphatic system has lymph vessels, lymphoid masses, lymph nodes and lymph, the fluid flowing in it (11.5).

book_ref.quote: It consists of lymph vessels, lymphoid masses, lymph nodes

blocks.prompt: 118 Lymph capillaries, where the lymphatic system begins, have:
blocks.explanation: The lymphatic system begins with lymph capillaries having blind endings in extracellular (interstitial) fluid (11.5).

book_ref.quote: which have blind endings in extracellular fluid

blocks.prompt: 119 Larger molecules can enter lymph capillaries because lymph capillaries:

options.text: are connected directly to the heart
are more permeable than blood capillaries

blocks.explanation: Lymph capillaries are more permeable than blood capillaries, so larger molecules can enter them (11.5).

book_ref.quote: Lymph capillaries are more permeable than blood capillaries.

blocks.prompt: 120 The thoracic duct opens into the:
blocks.explanation: The right lymphatic duct and the thoracic duct open into the right and left subclavian veins respectively (11.5).

book_ref.quote: These vessels open into right and left subclavian veins

blocks.prompt: 121 The flow of lymph towards the thoracic duct is maintained by:

options.text: the pumping of the heart alone
skeletal muscle activity, movement of viscera and breathing movements

blocks.explanation: Lymph flow is maintained by skeletal muscle activity, movement of viscera and breathing; valves prevent backflow (11.5).

book_ref.quote: It is maintained by the activity of skeletal muscles

blocks.prompt: 122 The branches of lymph capillaries in the villi are called:
blocks.explanation: Lymph capillary branches in villi are lacteals; chylomicrons enter them (11.5).

book_ref.quote: The branches of lymph capillaries in villi, are called lacteals.

blocks.prompt: 123 Chylomicrons that enter the lacteals are formed when:
blocks.explanation: Fatty acids and glycerol form triglycerides in villus cells; these are coated with proteins to form chylomicrons (11.5).

book_ref.quote: The triglycerides are coated with proteins to form chylomicrons

blocks.prompt: 124 The painful swelling of lymph nodes in diseases like mumps is largely due to:

options.text: accumulation of dead lymphocytes and macrophages

blocks.explanation: Painful swelling of lymph nodes in diseases such as mumps is largely due to accumulation of dead lymphocytes and macrophages (11.5).

book_ref.quote: accumulation of dead lymphocytes and macrophages

blocks.prompt: 125 Lymph enters a lymph node through several afferent vessels and leaves through:
blocks.explanation: Several afferent lymph vessels enter a lymph node and a single efferent vessel drains it (11.5).

book_ref.quote: the lymph is drained by a single efferent lymph vessel

blocks.prompt: 126 In man, lymph nodes are present in the:
blocks.explanation: Lymph nodes are present in the neck, axilla (armpit) and groin areas (11.5).

book_ref.quote: Lymph nodes are present in the neck region, axilla and groin areas of man.

blocks.prompt: 127 Which of these is one of the larger lymphoid masses?
blocks.explanation: The larger lymphoid masses are the spleen, thymus, tonsils and adenoids; they produce lymphocytes (11.5).

book_ref.quote: The larger lymphoid masses are spleen, thymus, tonsils and adenoids.

blocks.prompt: 128 In an average person, the excess fluid that leaves blood capillaries daily and is returned by the lymphatic system is about:
blocks.explanation: About three litres more fluid leaves blood capillaries daily; lymph capillaries absorb it and return it to the bloodstream (11.5).

book_ref.quote: about three litres more fluid leaves blood capillaries daily

blocks.prompt: 129 The spleen filters blood through macrophages and lymphocytes that destroy foreign particles and aged RBCs, and also:
blocks.explanation: The spleen filters blood, destroying foreign particles and aged RBCs, and also stores RBCs (11.5).

book_ref.quote: Spleen also functions to store RBCs.
